endorsements.quote: System design must leave space for professional override and explanation.

At the organizational level, continuing professional development must address the specific systems nurses encounter in their practice contexts, using case‐based and simulation approaches to model the epistemic‐to‐moral deference migration this paper identifies.
Moral agency does not require rejection of technological mediation.

unlisted_practices: Integrate ethics education oriented toward technology-mediated moral environments into pre-licensure nursing curricula.
Educate nurses to cultivate moral perception, critical interpretive capacity, and ethical confidence to question, contest, and override AI guidance without perceiving it as deviant.
Design governance structures that make interpretive override visible and legitimate and treat reasoned contestation as ethical engagement rather than non-conformity.
Engage nurses as moral stakeholders and participants in the design, implementation, and governance of clinical AI systems.
Provide regulatory frameworks with explicit legal protection for documented, reasoned override of AI recommendations, not only penalties for nonadherence.
Treat phronetic judgement as an assessable professional competency and avoid evaluating nursing practice solely through compliance dashboards and adherence to system pathways.

screen.reason: This is a theoretical and conceptual framework paper addressing nursing moral agency, responsibility, and boundary-setting in technology- and AI-mediated clinical care.
